stem: Which of the following injuries would require the application of a long leg or long arm cast rather than a short cast?

options.text: Buckle fractures of the distal radius.
Salter-Harris type fractures of the ankle.
Fractures involving the bones of the foot.

explanation: Fractures occurring in the shaft (diaphysis) of long bones require the stability provided by a long cast that extends above the joint proximal to the injury.
rationale: Focus on the location of the fracture relative to the mid-shaft of the bone.

optionExplanations.A: Fractures occurring in the shaft (diaphysis) of long bones require the stability provided by a long cast that extends above the joint proximal to the injury.
optionExplanations.B: These are stable, distal injuries that are adequately managed with a short arm cast.
optionExplanations.C: As distal injuries, these are categorized under those suitable for short leg immobilization.
optionExplanations.D: Distal injuries of the hand and foot only require immobilization that does not need to cross the knee or elbow.

source.hint: Focus on the location of the fracture relative to the mid-shaft of the bone.
